title: Core Residence: hotel-style TRX living, a step from the spotlight.
excerpt: A luxury residence at the edge of the TRX financial district, linked to the mall but facing away from it, where a 925 sq ft unit now lists at about RM2.2 million.
takeaways: Seven units a floor, three lifts, marble and bronze finishes, and links between towers.
A 925 sq ft two-plus-one unit lists at about RM2.2 million and rents for about RM7,800.
Years of construction next door, confusing road access, and finishes that fall short at this price.

sections.heading: What sets it apart
paragraphs: Core Residence sits on Jalan Barat at the edge of Tun Razak Exchange, linked to the TRX mall by an elevated bridge but with its entrances facing away from the district's centre. Each tower has its own lobby with a concierge, and floors have seven units sharing three lifts, with marble, timber panels and bronze trims. Fire corridors link the towers, so residents can use the next tower's lifts if their own fail.

Sean viewed a 925 sq ft two-plus-one unit with no balcony and no corridor inside, 3.1 m ceilings and near-full-height windows facing the TRX park. It comes with a fitted kitchen and appliances, centralised aircon and a smart lock. A rooftop gym and lap pool look out over Merdeka 118 and the TRX towers.

sections.heading: Where it is
paragraphs: TRX is the new financial district, with the Exchange TRX mall, its park and office towers next door, and highways routed into the master plan. Old shop lots, eateries and a community centre sit across the road. Empty plots around are being developed, and the MRT station is a walk through the mall.

sections.heading: Rent and returns
paragraphs: Subsale listings put this unit at about RM2.2 million, close to TRX Residences, and Sean notes prices have risen in the six or seven months since his last visit. Fully furnished, similar units ask about RM7,800 a month, three-bedrooms about RM9,000. The target, he says, is senior managers working next door.

pros: The TRX location: the new financial hub where jobs concentrate, which other transit-linked projects measure their distance to, with roads, rail and a government-backed master plan.
The micro location: connected to TRX but more private than TRX Residences, with its entrance facing away from the district and old shop lots and markets within walking distance.

Design: step-free routes from the street, separate lobbies, links between towers, an efficient layout with high ceilings, a park view that hides the city's busyness, and a rooftop gym facing five landmark towers.
cons: The micro site: empty plots alongside and opposite, so three to seven years of construction, more supply, and lost views.
Access: highways lead into TRX, but finding the building by car is confusing; Sean parked in the mall and walked over, and visitors will do the same.

Details that matter at RM2.2 million: an uneven kitchen backsplash, no foyer, a door that opens awkwardly against the shoe cabinet, a small pool, mid-range gym equipment and visible workmanship flaws. TRX Residences is the natural comparison.

closing: Sean calls the owner's pick awesome for living, but says that at this price buyers have many other choices and must be clear why they want this one.
sourceNote: Based on Sean's full English captions for this February 2026 episode. The 3 on 3 follows the three things he likes and the three he doesn't, in his order, at the end of the video. An owner let Sean view the completed unit; prices and rents are from property portal listings. A price-per-square-foot figure and some rents in the captions are unclear, so they are left out.
